r.정치 구도: Somalia is a federation made up of a federal government and several member states. After the central government collapsed in 1991 the country went through a long civil war, and the current federal government was only set up in 2012. Since then the president has been chosen by parliament rather than by voters, and members of parliament have been picked by delegates named by clan elders. Saying it wants to move to direct elections, the government amended the constitution in 2024 and again in March 2026, and in the process lengthened the terms of the president and parliament from four years to five. Puntland and Jubaland cut ties with the federal government, saying the changes were made without consensus, and the opposition wants to keep indirect elections through clan representatives. In November 2026 the Supreme Court ruled that the president's term had already ended in May, but the government refused to accept the ruling, leaving a constitutional crisis over who holds legitimate power.

t.why: Somalia sits at the mouth of the Gulf of Aden, which links the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean, so ships using the Suez Canal pass off its coast. When piracy surged in the late 2000s, navies from many countries arrived; attacks faded for years, then rose again around 2023, when Yemen's Houthi rebels were attacking ships in the Red Sea. The al-Qaeda-linked group al-Shabaab holds rural areas in the south and center and carries out bombings in the capital, and African Union troops have been backing the government since 2007. Somaliland in the northwest declared independence in 1991 and has governed itself since. Relations with Ethiopia soured badly after Ethiopia signed a memorandum with Somaliland in 2024 that would let it build a naval base on the Somaliland coast, and when Israel became the first country to recognize Somaliland in December 2025, the African Union and the Arab League objected. Turkey runs a large military training base in the capital, one sign of how Turkey and the Gulf states compete for influence there.
t.rel: Somaliland in the north has declared independence and governs itself; in 2025 Israel became the first country to recognize it. Somalia fights the Islamist group al-Shabaab with support from African Union troops, and there is tension with Ethiopia, which wants access to the sea.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1987. After a string of Korean ships were hijacked off Somalia in 2008, South Korea sent the navy's Cheonghae Unit to the Gulf of Aden in March 2009. The unit takes its name from Cheonghaejin, the maritime base built by Jang Bogo in the ninth century. It became widely known in January 2011 for Operation Dawn of Gulf of Aden, which rescued the crew of the hijacked Samho Jewelry. The unit still escorts Korean ships through these waters, and in July 2026 it responded to a distress call from a tanker boarded by armed men. Trade between the two countries remains small.
t.know: Somalia has the longest coastline of any country on the African mainland.
etext: Herding has long been the main livelihood, with camels, goats and sheep sold to Gulf countries such as Saudi Arabia. Money sent home by Somalis abroad, together with aid, keeps the economy afloat.

When the banks collapsed, telecom companies built mobile money services, and today even street vendors take payment by phone. Long use of the US dollar means dollars are more common than the local currency.

In December 2023 Somalia completed the final stage of the debt relief program for heavily indebted poor countries and had most of its foreign debt written off. That opened the way to new loans from international lenders.
Al-Shabaab collects tolls on rural roads while government tax revenue is very small. Droughts and floods alternate and often kill livestock in large numbers, and electricity and roads are scarce.
